newsitem.title: UK: Statoil still seeking shipping partner - chief exe.
newsitem.headline: Statoil still seeking shipping partner - chief exe.

text.p: Norway's state-owned oil company, Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap AS (Statoil ), is pressing ahead with its search for a joint venture partner for its shipping arm, Statoil's president and chief executive officer Harald Norvik said on Thursday.

Statoil's Shipping and Maritime Technology (SMT) division, the world's largest operator of offshore tankers with 19 shuttle tankers and nine conventional vessels, could be merged with a Norwegian or foreign company.
"We are now in the negotiating phase with both Norwegian and international companies, both shipowners and contracting companies," Norvik told a meeting of the Norwegian British Chamber of Commerce.

"It remains to be seen what the outcome of this is but we see this as a very interesting strategy... This is a business development which is right for Statoil and right for the owner," he said, countering suggestions that the company's state ownership could prove an obstacle.

Norvik said the same thinking that drove Statoil to merge its petrochemicals activities in 1994 with Finland's Neste, creating the Borealis joint venture, lay behind the search for a shipping partner.
SMT said on Monday it had ordered three new shuttle tankers from Spain's Astilleros Espanoles SA (Aesa) to cope with rising crude output on the Norwegian continental shelf.
